newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Bank of Namibia dismisses criticism on fx controls.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Namibia dismisses criticism on fx controls.

text.p: The Bank of Namibia said on Thursday that criticism of its decision not to introduce foreign currency accounts for local residents was unjustified given the current economic climate.
"The issue is not whether Namibian residents will be allowed to open foreign currency accounts, but rather when Namibian economic conditions will allow this," it said in a statement.
Last week the bank said it had no plans to allow local individuals to hold foreign currency accounts as such a move would exert undue influence on Namibia's balance of payments.

The decision has been criticised by some market analysts, who said this would send a bad signal to foreign investors and would not deter Namibians with assets in South Africa from making use of the foreign exchange control relaxations announced by the South African authorities.
On July 1, the South African Reserve Bank allowed local individuals to invest up to 200,000 rand offshore for the first time in 31 years.

"The current decision not to introduce foreign currency accounts for private individuals resident in Namibia should not be construed as a contradiction of the Bank's stated commitment to progressive exchange control relaxation," the Bank of Namibia said.

"A consistent and cautious approach is seen as the most effective means of instilling confidence in the international investment community, whereas a hasty implementation of unsustainable measures which may have to be reversed would send contradicting and damaging signals."

It defended its decision to allow institutions to invest offshore by saying the step was "more crucial in terms of enhancing international investor confidence and promoting foreign investment on the NSE and the diversification of risk".

In April this year, the Bank of Namibia announced liberalisation measures for institutional investors and direct foreign investment in Southern African Development Community countries which it said showed it was working towards exchange control liberalisation. -- Windhoek Newsroom +2646 1 245-260
